messages:
sara.h: FYI support just escalated: multiple customers (one high-traffic tenant) seeing 503s and long tail timeouts hitting hosted inference since ~14:02 UTC
miguel: I'm seeing a correlated uptick in 5xx from gateway metrics starting 14:01, primarily eu-west and us-east regions, overall error rate ~2-4% for a short window
oncall-bot: Incident created: INCIDENT-20240205-503WARMUP by sara.h
support-agent: customer report: spikes when they send long-generation requests (seq ~1200-1500), shorter requests seem ok
priya: any recent deploys between 13:45-14:15? I don't see app deploys in that window
tom: no infra deploys on my side. I can repro a 503 by replaying one of their traces through the gateway trace id=gw-ff33
alex: pasted gateway error sample:
```
2024-02-05T14:03:12Z gateway ERROR upstream response 503 route=/v1/chat.generate id=gw-ff33 err="read tcp 10.1.2.3:443: connection reset by peer"
```
miguel: model hosts are showing a burst of long-lived KV cache growth and some connection resets, looks like memory pressure on a subset of pods
sara.h: customer was doing a scheduled warmup — ramped from 30rps -> 250rps over ~90s per support notes
priya: also noticed intermittent 502s from identity at ~14:00 which caused a few token refresh failures — could be compounding backpressure
tom: quick mitigation: can we route this customer to a protected/dedicated pool while we debug? Need to avoid user impact
miguel: manually flipped routing for tenant-id 4321 -> dedicated-pool-a :white_check_mark:
oncall-bot: Routing update applied: tenant=4321 -> dedicated-pool-a by miguel
alex: runtime logs show repeated kv-cache stalls on model-node-9, GC spikes and then backend closes connections; saving full traces to s3://redwood-incidents/1709876543-warmup-logs
support-agent: relaying to customer: "We've routed you to an isolated pool and are investigating. Sorry for the disruption. You may see improved stability in the fallback pool."
customer: thanks, we see fewer 503s on the fallback. We'll keep sending traffic for now
miguel: immediate mitigation applied: reduced gateway prefix batching and lowered batch token cap to reduce per-pod memory: `batch.max_tokens=640, batch.window_ms=30` — rolling now
priya: can we also add temporary rate-limits for extremely long sequences as a safety valve? Policy question but helpful short-term
tom: added a temporary ingress throttle rule for seq_length > 1024 for the tenant at the gateway (60s cooldown) — monitoring impact
sara.h: proposed postmortem outline:
- trigger: scheduled warmup/ramp of long-generation traffic -> sudden per-pod memory growth and connection resets
- contributing: identity 502s caused token refresh retries and amplified load on gateway and backends
- immediate mitigations: routed traffic to dedicated pool; adjusted gateway batching; applied short-term throttle
- follow-ups & owners:
  - miguel: auto-detect long-gen ramp per-tenant and auto-failover to protected pools (ETA 4d)
  - alex: deep-dive into kv-cache growth and GC behavior on model-node-9 (ETA 5d)
  - priya: coordinate with identity team to reduce 502s and harden token refresh retries/backoff (ETA 2d)
  - tom: add playbook entry for warmup/ramp procedures and tenant-isolation steps (ETA 3d)
  - sara.h: draft customer-facing postmortem and communicate SLAs/next steps (ETA 2d)
miguel: I'll also create an alert: sustained connection_reset_count > 30/min on any model node -> Pager
alex: exporting metrics dashboards & logs to incident bucket and tagging traces with tenant=4321
priya: action: review default batching profiles to be safer for long-gen workloads (owner: priya + eng-runtime, ETA 7d)
sara.h: good. schedule a follow-up check-in in 90 minutes to validate mitigations and confirm routing stability :thumbsup:
